audits.title: 1494 An Audit on The Management of Adhesional Small Bowel Obstruction at St Helier Hospital
audits.standard: BMJ Best Practice ASBO algorithm and National Audit of Small Bowel Obstruction 2017
audits.setting: General surgical take, St Helier Hospital

cycle1.result: IV fluids 100%; analgesia 34 (97.1%); anti-emetics 31 (88.6%); NG tube 21 (82.9%); conservative trial 30 (85.7%), water-soluble contrast 24 (80%); 8 (36.3%) failed conservative management and had laparotomy within 70 hours.

audits.other_findings: 5 (14.3%) had laparotomy within 37 hours of admission; a step-by-step flow chart at induction is proposed.
audits.citation: Rivera Cartland M, Anjum Z, Saadat S, Studd T, Camprodon R. 1494 An Audit on The Management of Adhesional Small Bowel Obstruction at St Helier Hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.165.

audits.title: EP.FRI.758 Management of Small Bowel Obstruction: A Retrospective Audit
audits.standard: BMJ Best Practice algorithm and National Audit of Small Bowel Obstruction (NASBO) recommendations
audits.setting: District general hospital in London (St George's, Epsom and St Helier, Kingston)

cycle1.result: All but one had CT, 90% within 12 hours of assessment; 64% of conservatively managed patients received a water-soluble study.

audits.other_findings: Seven had immediate surgery within 12 hours; of 5 who failed conservative management only one was operated on after 72 hours.
audits.citation: Baggaley A, Clements C, Tudyka V. EP.FRI.758 Management of Small Bowel Obstruction: A Retrospective Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab312.116.

audits.title: 482 A closed loop audit showing learning from the National Audit of Small Bowel Obstruction at a District General Hospital
audits.standard: National Audit of Small Bowel Obstruction (NASBO) recommendations: early CT, water-soluble contrast, early nutritional assessment and specialist input
audits.setting: District general hospital, Antrim Area Hospital

cycle1.result: CT 88%; water-soluble contrast 12%; average days to CT 0.18; no oral intake >5 days 44%; parenteral nutrition 6%.

audits.intervention: Findings presented at an audit and governance meeting, reiterating NASBO recommendations.

cycle2.result: CT 94%; water-soluble contrast 44%; average days to CT 0.43; no oral intake >5 days 17%; parenteral nutrition 17%.

audits.other_findings: AXR plus CT rose from 75% to 88%; nutritional assessment did not improve (malnourished identified 6% then 5%).
audits.citation: Mallon A, Gallagher C. 482 A closed loop audit showing learning from the National Audit of Small Bowel Obstruction at a District General Hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad241.501.

audits.title: 905 To Operate or Not to Operate? a Clinical Audit in the Management of Adhesional Small Bowel Obstruction
audits.standard: National audit of small bowel obstruction 2017 and Bologna guidelines

cycle1.result: IV fluids 100%; analgesia 38 (88.4%); anti-emetics 36 (83.7%); NG tube 21 (72.1%); 37% of conservatively managed patients received water-soluble contrast; average time to theatre 4 days (96 hours).

audits.other_findings: Contrast led to resolution in 20 patients (83.3%); an ASBO flow chart is proposed.
audits.citation: Karagiannidis G, Khaliq T, El-Farran M, Youssef F. 905 To Operate or Not to Operate? a Clinical Audit in the Management of Adhesional Small Bowel Obstruction. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.368.

audits.title: 1309 A Quality Improvement Project on Small Bowel Obstruction Operative Mortality Rate
audits.standard: ASGBI and NCEPOD recommendations on small bowel obstruction management
audits.setting: Watford General Hospital, emergency laparotomy cases (NELA data)

cycle1.result: 198 emergency laparotomies with 24 mortalities (12%); 87 SBO cases with 12 mortalities (SBO operative mortality 14%); SBO accounted for 50% of emergency laparotomy deaths.

audits.intervention: SBO management flowchart and allocation of a theatre slot within 72 hours for patients suitable for operation.

cycle2.result: 152 emergency laparotomies with 13 mortalities (9%); 57 SBO cases with 3 mortalities (SBO operative mortality 5%); SBO-related deaths 23% of emergency laparotomy deaths.

audits.citation: Azri Yahaya A, Hollingshead J. 1309 A Quality Improvement Project on Small Bowel Obstruction Operative Mortality Rate. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.551.

audits.title: FP7.7 - Evaluation of small bowel obstruction management: A local audit in comparison to NASBO guidelines
audits.standard: National Audit of Small Bowel Obstruction (NASBO) recommendations
audits.setting: Conquest Hospital, East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust / Medway Maritime Hospital

cycle1.result: CT on admission 98.3% (NASBO 80%), average time to CT 9 hours; surgery 27% with average time to surgery 2.4 days (NASBO 1 day); nutritional screening 100% (NASBO 90%).

audits.other_findings: 30-day mortality 14% (NASBO 8%) and 30-day readmission 18% (NASBO 13%) despite shorter length of stay (7 vs 10.7 days).
audits.citation: Holt T, Rana S, Wu F. FP7.7 - Evaluation of small bowel obstruction management: A local audit in comparison to NASBO guidelines. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae197.405.
